newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos orders the renegotiation of the joint venture agreement with Amari Bay Coastal Development Corp (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The People's Intiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action, the group pushing for the lifting of the presidential term, is asking the Supreme Court to reconsider its decision declaring their initiative illegal. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- President Fidel Ramos dismisses reports that there is a split in the ruling coalition party over the senatorial slate. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Switzerland wants the Philippines to negotiate with human rights victims and other claimants to the assets of Ferdinand Marcos to determine who should keep the $500 million deposit of the Marcoses in two Swiss banks. (TODAY)
- Bank treasurers have cautioned against any further decline in the local interest rates which might prompt foreign funds to pull out. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The International Monetary Fund has projected the Philippines will attain one of the highest export growth rates within the Asia Pacific region this year. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Creditors of Victorias Milling Co Inc may take over the sugar milling firm as part of its restructuring programme, Urban Bank president Arsenio Bartolome says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Cosmos Bottling Corp says it has the second biggest market share in the softdrinks business in the Philippines, behind Coca-Cola. (MANILA TIMES)
